newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech ruling party takes lead in Senate polls.
newsitem.headline: Czech ruling party takes lead in Senate polls.

text.p: The party of right-wing Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus took a solid early lead in Senate election run-offs on Saturday, but turnout was dismal despite an appeal to vote from President Vaclav Havel.

With results from slightly more than a quarter of the 81 constituencies declared, Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) won 12 seats in the new upper house, ahead of the opposition Social Democrats with four.
The Christian Democrats, a junior partner in Klaus's centre-right coalition, won three seats and the third party in the government, the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA) won one.

No overall turnout figure was available but an official of the Central Election Commission said that it had been even lower than the 35 percent recorded in the first round of the Senate polls on November 15 and 16.
Before the second round, Havel appealed to Czechs to turn out in far greater numbers for the sake of the credibility of the new upper house, but in some constituencies it was less than 30 percent.

The Senate elections had been billed as key to the future of Klaus's coalition, which lost its lower house majority in elections six months ago. But analysts say that with turnout so low, the Senate results have little significance.
